capabilityIndex.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
capabilityIndex.attribution: Capability scores are published by Artificial Analysis and reproduced with attribution.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.note: OpenAI's frontier model, released 3 September 2026. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Prompts with more than 272K input tokens use the standard long-context column on the pricing page: $20 input / $2 cached / $75 output for the whole request.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.note: OpenAI labels the published $4 input / $0.40 cached / $20 output rate as promotional pricing available at least through November 21, 2026. The pricing page does not state a separate post-promotion standard rate, so that published rate stays the headline. Prompts above 272K input tokens use the pricing table's long-context column, $8 input / $0.80 cached / $30 output, for the whole request. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.note: Published short-context rate is $2 input / $0.20 cached / $12 output. The model page states that prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and 1.5x output for the full request. The long-context input ($4) and output ($18) are derived from that multiplier applied to the published $2 / $12 rates. The model page does not state a long-context cached rate, so this band keeps the published cached rate of $0.20. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.note: Published short-context rate is $0.20 input / $0.02 cached / $1.20 output. The model page states that prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and 1.5x output for the full request. The long-context input ($0.40) and output ($1.80) are derived from that multiplier applied to the published $0.20 / $1.20 rates. The model page does not state a long-context cached rate, so this band keeps the published cached rate of $0.02. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.note: Frontier reasoning and agentic model; succeeds Opus 4.8. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.note: Cache hits and refreshes are priced at 0.025x base input ($0.25 / 1M) instead of the usual 0.1x. Supersedes Claude Fable 5.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.note: Permanent standard rate ($2 input / $10 output / $0.20 cached). Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.note: Prices unchanged at $1 input / $0.10 cache read / $5 output. The Sonnet 5.5 model comparison lists a 200K context window and 64K maximum output (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/overview). The models overview lists Claude Haiku 4.5 among Legacy models that remain available (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview). The deprecations table lists claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 as Active, with retirement not sooner than October 15, 2026 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations). Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.note: Standard price shown for prompts up to 200K tokens (inclusive). Prompts above 200K bill $4 input, $0.40 cached input, and $18 output per million tokens. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.note: Standard rate shown. An introductory rate of $0.75 input / $0.075 cached / $3.75 output runs through December 31, 2026. 1M input limit with 64K max output.

models.name: Grok 4.6
models.note: Prompts at or above 200K use $4 input, $1 cached input, and $12 output per million tokens. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Grok 4.5
models.note: Prompts at or above 200K use $4 input, $0.60 cached input, and $12 output per million tokens. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Grok Build 0.1
models.note: Agentic coding and tool-calling model. Prompts at or above 200K tokens use $2 input, $0.40 cached input, and $4 output per million tokens for the whole request. Context window is 256K. Artificial Analysis has no model page for this model, so Intelligence Index v5.0 does not score it (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
models.note: Input and output are the published peak rates ($1.32 in / $3.96 out). Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday; all other hours bill at half those rates ($0.66 in / $1.98 out). The cached rate is not a published figure: it is a time-weighted blend of the $0.044 peak and $0.022 off-peak cache-hit rates, weighted by the 35 peak and 133 off-peak hours in a week.

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.note: Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Codestral
models.note: Specialized model for code generation and Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM) workflows. Mistral publishes no cached input rate for it, so cache reads are priced at the full input rate. The catalog previously carried $0.03, which appears on no Mistral page. Artificial Analysis has no model page for this model, so Intelligence Index v5.0 does not score it (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.note: Flagship 1M context model; available through GLM Coding Plan and OpenCode Zen.

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
models.note: Standard rate shown; the 50% promotional rate that ran through September 9, 2026 has ended. Cached input storage is free for a limited time. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Kimi K3
models.note: Also available through OpenCode Zen; web search is billed separately. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Kimi K2.7 Code
models.note: Coding-specialized API; not ranked for general writing or research. Kimi's pricing page says K2 series models are closed to newly registered users from October 31, 2026, and all K2 series models are planned to retire by the end of December 2026 (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat). Existing users are unaffected until then. The row stays because OpenCode Go, Go Plus, and Zen still list it. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: Muse Spark 1.3
models.note: Standard tier, not used to improve Meta products. A contributor tier (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) costs $0.10 input / $0.002 cached / $0.20 output in exchange for allowing Meta to train on prompts and outputs.

models.name: Qwen3.8-Max
models.note: International (Singapore) endpoint rate. The Beijing, US, Germany, Japan, and Hong Kong endpoints bill lower at $1.65 input / $0.206 cached / $4.951 output. Max input is 991,808 tokens of the 1M window.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
models.note: Replaces DeepSeek V4 Flash; called as `deepseek-flash`, and the legacy `deepseek-v4-flash` identifier still routes here at Flash pricing. Input and output are the published peak rates ($0.30 in / $1.20 out). Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday; all other hours bill at half those rates ($0.15 in / $0.60 out). The cached rate is not a published figure: it is a time-weighted blend of the $0.006 peak and $0.003 off-peak cache-hit rates, weighted by the 35 peak and 133 off-peak hours in a week. Maximum output is 384K tokens. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score on https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/deepseek-v4-1-flash (checked 2026-10-29). The separate snapshot page https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017 scores 32 and is not this row.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.note: Released 21 September 2026 at Grok 4.6 prices. Prompts at or above 200K use $4 input, $1 cached input, and $12 output per million tokens. A fast variant, available through Cursor and Grok Build only, serves output at twice the speed for twice the price.

models.name: Step 5 Preview
models.note: StepFun's flagship agentic model, released 18 September 2026. Sparse mixture-of-experts with text, image and video input. Re-read October 19, 2026 from the pricing page: $1 input, $0.10 cache hit, and $2.70 output per million tokens. Maximum output is 64K tokens, and output tokens include the reasoning trace. The cache-miss input price covers writing new content to the cache.

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.note: Succeeds Opus 5 at a lower price. Cache reads are 0.05x input rather than Anthropic's usual 0.1x. The full 1M window is billed at standard rates; fast mode ($8 / $40) is a separate premium tier, not the headline rate.

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
models.note: GPT-6 mid tier, built for complex coding and agentic work. Half the published GPT-5.6 Sol price. Maximum output is 128K tokens. The model page states that prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the whole request. The long-context band ($4 input / $0.40 cached / $15 output) is derived from that multiplier applied to the published $2 / $0.20 / $10 rates. The pricing table does not list a separate long-context row for this model. Artificial Analysis does not publish an Intelligence Index v5.0 score for this model (checked 2026-10-29).

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.note: OpenAI's most efficient GPT-6 model, for focused, high-volume tasks. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Prompts with more than 272K input tokens use the standard long-context column: $0.20 input / $0.02 cached / $0.75 output for the whole request.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.note: Newer Sol model, described by OpenAI as near-Astra performance for complex work at a lower cost. Same input and output rates as GPT-6 Sol with half the cached rate. GPT-6 Sol remains available. Maximum output is 128K tokens. Prompts with more than 272K input tokens use the standard long-context column: $4 input / $0.20 cached / $15 output for the whole request.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
models.note: Released September 28, 2026. Cache reads were cut from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens on October 7, 2026 (0.05x base input). 5-minute cache writes stay $2.50 and 1-hour cache writes stay $4. The Batch API is 50% off input and output. US-only inference is 1.1x. Retirement is not sooner than September 28, 2027. Maximum output is 128K tokens on the synchronous API.

models.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
models.note: Released October 7, 2026. Prompts up to 100,000 tokens are $0.10 input / $0.01 cache read / $0.50 output; prompts over 100,000 tokens are $0.50 / $0.05 / $2.50 for the whole request. 5-minute cache writes are $0.125 below that line and $0.625 above it; 1-hour cache writes are $0.20 and $1. The Batch API is 50% off input and output. Synchronous maximum output is 128K tokens; the Message Batches API allows 300K with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header. Retirement is not sooner than October 7, 2027.

models.name: Mistral Large 4
models.note: Public Preview since October 6, 2026. Open-weight Mixture-of-Experts. The model card shows only the standard rate, $1.36 input / $0.14 cached / $4.18 output. The earlier 2-week 50% launch sale is no longer on the page (https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large-4-0).

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon
models.note: GA October 13, 2026. Standard rate from December 1, 2026 shown. An introductory rate of $2 input / $0.10 cached / $10 output runs through November 30, 2026. Implicit caching only (explicit caching not supported). One published rate applies across the full context window. Batch and Flex are 50% of standard; Priority is 1.8×. Context window is 1,048,576 tokens. Default synchronous max output is 65,536; long decode / background execution raises the hard ceiling to 1,048,576, and maxOutputTokens records that ceiling at the catalog 1M context bound. Sources: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing and https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-4-argon.

models.name: Muse Wonder
models.note: Announced October 12, 2026. API id `muse-wonder-1.0`. Standard mode only on Model API; Contributor mode is not available for Muse Wonder on Model API. One published rate applies across the full window. The models page states a 1,048,576-token context window, recorded as 1.048576M. Muse Wonder Full is available only with a Muse Code subscription and has no public API price, so it is not listed. Muse Code High Usage ($15), Power Usage ($50), and Maximum Usage ($200) include Muse Wonder; Everyday Usage is $5 and stays under the catalog floor (https://dev.meta.ai/help/subscriptions/what-is-a-muse-code-subscription). The separate Muse agent Power ($20) and Maximum ($100) plans name a weekly token allowance and do not name this model (https://www.meta.com/help/subscriptions/1021145227643680/). Meta One plan pages describe consumer AI usage and do not name it (https://www.meta.com/meta-one-plans/).

models.name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
models.note: GA October 19, 2026. API id `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`. Early anonymous serving was Space Bunny. Thinking depth is tunable through effort (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; default `max`). Multimodal: text, image, and video input. The model guide states a 1,000,000-token context window. Prompt-cache reads are $0.015 per million tokens.

models.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
models.note: Released October 23, 2026. API id `kimi-k3.1-pro`. One published rate applies across the full window. The pricing page states a 1,048,576-token context window, recorded as 1.048576M. Kimi bills cache misses, cache writes, and cache hits as separate slices of the same input tokens. The default 5-minute cache write is $2 per million tokens, the same as input, and the caching guide says that write was already included in the input price, so the stored input and cached rates cover the default. The optional 1-hour cache write is $4 per million tokens (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/context-caching). The separate id `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` is not listed. Kimi K3 remains the previous-generation model. Quickstart default max completion tokens is 131,072 and can be set up to 1,048,576. Sources: https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat , https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart , and https://www.kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro .

models.name: GPT-6.1 Terra
models.note: Released October 26, 2026. Published short-context rate is $1 input / $0.05 cached / $5 output. The model page states that prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the full request. The long-context band ($2 input / $0.10 cached / $7.50 output) is derived from that multiplier applied to the published $1 / $0.05 / $5 rates. 30-minute cache writes are $1.25 per million tokens and 12-hour cache writes are $2.50. Maximum output is 128K tokens. GPT-5.6 Terra remains available. Sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-terra , https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing , and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog .
